newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ASTROS AND TIGERS MAKE NINE-PLAYER TRADE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ASTROS AND TIGERS MAKE NINE-PLAYER TRADE.

text.p: The Houston Astros and Detroit Tigers exchanged promising pitchers and position players in a nine-player deal Tuesday that was the biggest in the major leagues in two years.

Houston sent pitchers Todd Jones and Doug Brocail, outfielder Brian Hunter and shortstop Orlando Miller to Detroit for hurlers Trever Miller, Jose Lima and C.J. Nitkowski, catcher Brad Ausmus and infielder Daryle Ward.
Detroit will also receive a player to be named or cash considerations.

Jones has spent time as Houston's closer in each of the last two seasons, but bouts of ineffectiveness and injuries kept him from securing the job. The 28-year-old right-hander was 6-3 with 17 saves and a 4.40 ERA last season.
Orlando Miller, 27, is coming off his first full season as Houston's everyday shortstop. He batted .256 with 15 homers and 58 RBI.
Hunter, 25, hit .276 with five homers, 35 RBI and 35 stolen bases while showing good range in centre field.
The key to the deal for Houston was the 27-year-old Ausmus, a strong defensive catcher whose departure opens the way in Detroit for highly-regarded prospect Raul Casanova.
Ausmus, who came over from San Diego in a multi-player trade last season, batted a combined .221 with five homers and 35 RBI in 125 games.
"Acquiring a frontline catcher was a top priority for us," Houston general manager Gerry Hunsicker said. "Brad Ausmus is emerging as one of the top catchers in baseball."
Nitkowski and Trever Miller are both 23-year-old lefties, while Lima is a 24-year-old right-hander who was 4-5 last season.
